# Installation {#sec-install}

## Package

Install `sconjoint` from GitHub. It contains C++ code, so it needs a compiler: Xcode command-line
tools on macOS, Rtools on Windows, or a standard build toolchain on Linux.

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("xuyiqing/sconjoint")
```

The package needs R 4.1 or later and four packages: `Rcpp`, `withr`, `digest`, and `spacefillr`
(scrambled Sobol points for numerical integration). The book's figures use base R graphics.

```{r}
#| label: load
library(sconjoint)
packageVersion("sconjoint")
```

```{r}
#| label: render-revision
#| echo: false
rev <- tryCatch(system2("git", c("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE),
                error = function(e) character(0), warning = function(e) character(0))
rev <- if (length(rev)) rev[1] else "unknown"
```

This book was rendered with sconjoint `r packageVersion("sconjoint")`, from source revision
`r rev` of the package repository.

Two datasets ship with the package, `gs2020` [@graham2020democracy] and `br2017`
[@ballard2017structure]. `sc_example_data()` turns each into the paper's model inputs.

```{r}
#| label: data-list
data(package = "sconjoint")$results[, c("Item", "Title")]
```

## Saved fits

Fitting the model at the paper's settings takes hours. Most of the time goes to each held-out
respondent's information (@sec-inference), not to training the network. The paper's fold states
are saved in two files:

| File | Application | Taste factors | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gs_q3.rds` | Graham and Svolik (2020) | 3 | 42,951,896 bytes |
| `br_q4.rds` | Ballard-Rosa, Martin and Scheve (2017) | 4 | 20,506,732 bytes |

Their checksums:

- `gs_q3.rds`: MD5 `17d0f2efa2ecf7c4b2ce3b01991a893b`; SHA-256
  `82ec4e8005d2979f8352d65d3104ea6d503542be005ed1c352658819af845731`.
- `br_q4.rds`: MD5 `6293fd6938d20477369b4f583c986a43`; SHA-256
  `0aa879eadc4ed744ec508dd26fc7a85521326c3f8f8d107c03dd56e8fd245faa`.

The files are too large for the package. They are published with the GitHub release
[`fits-2026-11`](https://github.com/xuyiqing/sconjoint/releases/tag/fits-2026-11). For each of the
five folds, a file holds what `sc_estimate()` needs and the fold's network and covariate scaling. It
also holds the respondent ids, groups, folds, the validation respondents (used to stop training
early), and a checksum of its contents that `sc_load()` verifies.

To download both files into a folder `fits` and check them:

```{r}
#| label: fits-download
#| eval: false
base <- "https://github.com/xuyiqing/sconjoint/releases/download/fits-2026-11"
files <- c("gs_q3.rds", "br_q4.rds")
md5 <- c("17d0f2efa2ecf7c4b2ce3b01991a893b", "6293fd6938d20477369b4f583c986a43")
dir.create("fits", showWarnings = FALSE)
options(timeout = max(600, getOption("timeout")))
for (f in files) download.file(file.path(base, f), file.path("fits", f), mode = "wb")
unname(tools::md5sum(file.path("fits", files))) == md5   # both TRUE
```

**Provenance.** The fits are the paper's selected-rank fits. They were trained on 14 November 2026
at package revision `1f7567a` (in the repository's history), on the paper's inputs, which
`sc_example_data()` rebuilds exactly from the bundled data. The folds and validation respondents are
stored in the files. On 25
November 2026 each application's fold states and fit files were packed into one file with
`sc_save()`, under package version 0.4.0.9000. The packing was checked: `sc_load()` gives back fold
states identical to the originals, and each fold's stored network reproduces its stored mean tastes
exactly. The files keep these records (`package_version` and `fit_sha` inside each file). They
describe the archived fits, so they stay as they are; later package versions read the files
unchanged.

@sec-gs, @sec-br, @sec-inference and @sec-respondents read the files from the folder in the option
`sconjoint.fits`. The default is `fits` in the working directory. For another folder, set the
option first:

```{r}
#| label: fits-option
#| eval: false
options(sconjoint.fits = "~/Downloads/sconjoint-fits")
```

Each chapter runs in its own R session. To render the book with the fits elsewhere, put that line
in an `.Rprofile` file in the book's folder.

```{r}
#| label: fits-check
fits <- getOption("sconjoint.fits", "fits")
file.exists(file.path(fits, c("gs_q3.rds", "br_q4.rds")))
gs <- sc_load(file.path(fits, "gs_q3.rds"))
gs
```

The printout gives the rank $q$, the number of folds, respondents and coded features, and the
integration settings used for the information and the scores. `sc_load()` returns `NULL` with a message when the
file is missing. It stops when the checksum does not match.
